clay_bodies.name: Standard Stoneware
clay_bodies.description: General-purpose stoneware body suitable for throwing and handbuilding. Fires to a warm tan in oxidation, gray-brown in reduction.
clay_bodies.notes: Reliable workhorse body. Good plasticity and wide firing range.

clay_bodies.name: Porcelain - Grolleg-based
clay_bodies.description: English kaolin porcelain with excellent translucency and very white fired color. Grolleg kaolin provides superior plasticity for a porcelain.
clay_bodies.notes: Premium porcelain. Short working window on the wheel but excellent translucency. Low iron and titanium give very white fired color.

clay_bodies.name: Porcelain - Standard
clay_bodies.description: Classic high-fire porcelain using domestic kaolin and potash feldspar. Less plastic than Grolleg bodies but very reliable at cone 10.
clay_bodies.notes: Workable domestic porcelain. Slightly warmer fired color than Grolleg due to higher TiO2.

clay_bodies.name: B-Mix (Laguna)
clay_bodies.description: Laguna Clay's popular mid-fire throwing body. Smooth, light-colored stoneware with excellent plasticity and minimal warping.
clay_bodies.notes: Popular commercial body for cone 6. Light color shows glaze colors well. Very forgiving on the wheel.

clay_bodies.name: Flameware / Lithium Body
clay_bodies.description: Thermal-shock resistant body using petalite or spodumene as a lithium source. Suitable for stovetop cooking vessels.
clay_bodies.notes: Low thermal expansion due to lithium and magnesium content. Must use compatible low-expansion glazes. Not all glazes will fit.

clay_bodies.name: Raku Body
clay_bodies.description: Open, grog-heavy body designed to withstand the thermal shock of raku firing. High grog content provides porosity and resistance to cracking.
clay_bodies.notes: Not food safe due to high porosity. The open body withstands rapid temperature changes of raku firing without cracking.

clay_bodies.name: Red Earthenware
clay_bodies.description: Classic low-fire terracotta-style body. High iron content produces distinctive red-orange color. Traditional material for functional pottery and tile.
clay_bodies.notes: Must be glazed for food use due to porosity. Lovely warm color under clear or transparent glazes. Do not overfire past cone 2.

clay_bodies.name: White Earthenware
clay_bodies.description: Low-fire white body for majolica and bright-colored glazes. Low iron content for clean white surface.
clay_bodies.notes: White background ideal for majolica decoration. Talc acts as flux at low temperatures. Must be glazed for food use.

clay_bodies.name: Paper Clay - Porcelain
clay_bodies.description: Porcelain body with 5-15% paper fiber (cellulose) added. Provides extraordinary joining strength and crack resistance in construction. Paper burns out in bisque firing.
clay_bodies.notes: Paper fiber burns out during bisque, leaving tiny voids. Stronger in greenware and bone-dry state than regular porcelain. May smell during bisque.

clay_bodies.name: Wood-fire Stoneware
clay_bodies.description: Iron-bearing stoneware formulated for wood firing. Moderate iron shows beautiful flashing and ash interaction. Designed for cone 10-12 with heavy ash deposit.
clay_bodies.notes: Iron content creates orange-red flashing where exposed to flame. Ash deposits create natural glaze. May bloat if overfired past cone 12.

clay_bodies.name: Dark Stoneware / Manganese Body
clay_bodies.description: Dark-burning stoneware with added manganese dioxide and iron. Creates a chocolate-brown to nearly black fired body. Dramatic contrast under light-colored glazes.
clay_bodies.notes: Manganese can off-gas during firing - ensure good ventilation. Creates stunning contrast under white or light glazes that break on edges.

clay_bodies.name: Sculpture Body with Grog
clay_bodies.description: Heavily grogged sculpture body designed for large-scale work. High grog content reduces shrinkage and warping, provides structural support for thick walls.
clay_bodies.notes: Not suitable for throwing due to coarse grog. Low shrinkage minimizes cracking in thick or uneven forms. Can be left unglazed.

clay_bodies.name: Translucent Porcelain
clay_bodies.description: Ultra-refined high-fire porcelain optimized for translucency. Minimal iron and titanium impurities. When thrown or cast thin, transmits light.
clay_bodies.notes: Extremely high shrinkage demands careful drying. Pieces under 3mm thick will be translucent. Bone ash contributes to translucency and warm quality of light.

clay_bodies.name: Anagama Body
clay_bodies.description: Robust stoneware designed for extended anagama/noborigama kiln firings of 3-7 days. High alumina content resists warping during long firings.
clay_bodies.color_fired_reduction: gray-brown with orange flash, heavy ash glazing
clay_bodies.notes: High alumina prevents slumping during multi-day firings. Iron content provides warm flashing. Sand adds thermal shock resistance during stoking.

clay_bodies.name: Salt/Soda Stoneware
clay_bodies.description: Body formulated for salt or soda vapor glazing. Moderate alumina to develop the characteristic orange-peel texture when sodium reacts with the clay surface.
clay_bodies.notes: Alumina and silica in the body react with sodium vapor to form glaze in situ. Wadding required where pieces touch shelves. Slip decoration responds beautifully to salt/soda.
